acceptance: Published results include exact releases, corpus, models, hardware, failures, measured-versus-estimated labels, immutable existing vector-bakeoff receipt/config/input hashes, both host receipts, and explicit publication disposition; the completed vector bakeoff is not rerun.
observed: This task adds the whole-task benchmark harness and holdout protocol on top of the pre-existing MBR-804 receipt contract (benchmarks/task/mbr-804.v1.schema.json, scripts/qualification/verify-whole-task-benchmark.mjs — unmodified, imported read-only). benchmarks/whole-task/runner.mjs assembles a receipt matching that contract from: (1) exact release identity (40-hex commit, generation, client, service) and exact corpus identity (id, version, sha256, case count, an explicit fixture:true/false flag); (2) every model and macOS/Windows hardware description supplied by the caller; (3) an explicit failures array built from every non-success case, never inferred from absence; (4) metrics that are always {measured:true, value:<number>, unit:<string>} — task_success, context_errors, latency_ms, tokens, cache, cost — verified end to end in runner.test.mjs's failing-case test, which shows a failure surfaces in both failures[] and metrics.context_errors rather than being silently dropped; (5) benchmarks/whole-task/bakeoff-reference.mjs, which pins the sha256 of the vector bakeoff's config, input, and final receipt/report at authoring time and recomputes those hashes from the real, already-completed, un-rerun artifacts on disk on every call (bakeoff-reference.test.mjs proves this against the real files at docs/benchmarks/vector-backend/round1/{mac,windows}/receipt.json and fails closed — status mutated/missing — when a copy is tampered or absent; no cargo/python/rust process is ever spawned to produce these hashes); (6) benchmarks/whole-task/runner.mjs's writeHostReceipt()/hostReceiptPaths mechanism, which is this task's own 'both host receipts' (macOS and Windows), structurally mirroring MBR-801's per-platform receipt pattern, required and hash-checked before a non-fixture receipt can reach status complete (runner.test.mjs's end-to-end test constructs both with real hostname/arch identity and shows the resulting receipt.hosts.{macos,windows}.status is 'measured' and tied to the same release.generation); and (7) an explicit publication.{disposition, approved} field, defaulting to {not-published, false} and never auto-approving a published disposition. The whole-task corpus itself is a synthetic fixture (corpus.fixture.json, fixture:true) with no real product corpus available at task-implementation time; runner.mjs hard-guards in code (not only in documentation) that a fixture corpus can only ever produce status 'source-ready', never 'complete' — proven by runner.test.mjs's 'can never produce status complete' test — so no benchmark score is or can be fabricated by this task. Separately, benchmarks/whole-task/holdout.mjs implements the genuine holdout protocol required by the task title: a deterministic sha256(salt:caseId) bucket split (independently recomputable, not asserted) combined with a commit-reveal salt scheme (commitSalt/verifySaltCommitment) so the holdout boundary is pinned before a run and only checked against its pre-published commitment after — runner.mjs rejects any run whose revealed salt does not match its own pre-committed commitment. Status is recorded as pending_book_gate, not pass, per the book-mode execution rules: acceptance is finalized only at the Wave 3 phased gate (Gate phase 3.1) after node scripts/qualification/run.mjs --task MBR-804 is run there against a real release, a real corpus, and real per-platform host receipts.
